Bullous Pemphigoid: The presence of tense axillary bullae and linear C3 and IgG deposits along the basement membrane is characteristic of Bullous Pemphigoid.
Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita: Although less likely, the presence of bullae and immunofluorescence findings could also be seen in Epidermolysis Bullosa Acquisita, which also involves the basement membrane.
Linear IgA Bullous Dermatosis: This condition also presents with bullae and linear deposits along the basement membrane, but the specific immunofluorescence pattern and clinical context make it less likely than Bullous Pemphigoid.
Dermatitis Herpetiformis: This condition typically presents with itchy, blistering skin but is more associated with granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae rather than linear deposits along the basement membrane.
Pemphigus Vulgaris: Although it can present with bullae, the flaccid nature of the bullae and the location of the deposits within the epidermis rather than along the basement membrane make it less likely given the specific findings in this case.
